title: Distinguishing sets and measures from their planar Brownian images
abstract: Lean 4 formalisation of all 32 numbered statements of "Distinguishing sets and measures from their planar Brownian images" (Sascha Troscheit, arXiv:2610.16339), which asks whether two deterministic time measures on the unit interval can be distinguished almost surely from a single planar Brownian image. Rescaled correlation integrals of the time measures determine expected correlation profiles of the image measures, and profiles that differ in the limit make the image laws mutually singular, even when the time measures have the same dimension. For natural measures of self-similar sets satisfying the open set condition, renewal theory gives the profile asymptotics, a limit in the non-lattice case and a periodic non-constant limit in the lattice case, which separates lattice from non-lattice measures. Normalised neighbourhood measures of the compact Brownian image converge almost surely to the occupation measure, so the separation transfers to the laws of the compact image sets. In the two-contraction family of fixed dimension, the mean profile is real analytic and non-constant in the parameter, so each parameter is separated from all but finitely many others; for sufficiently small dimension the mean is strictly increasing and every pair of distinct parameters is separated. A homometric pair of self-similar measures with non-isometric attractors and identical profiles shows that the profile does not determine the measure. Renewal theory is proved for the self-similar laws used, and the nine headline results are stated over Mathlib alone and audited with Comparator.
